$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.util. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-UTIL-LINE-START-PREV
arms.note: the walk back tests the character at the position instead of the one before it, so a position that starts a line, or sits on a break, stops one early

arms.name: M-UTIL-LINE-START-CLAMP
arms.note: a position past the text no longer resolves to the last line

arms.name: M-UTIL-LINE-START-NEGATIVE
arms.note: a negative position is returned as it is instead of the text start

arms.name: M-UTIL-LINE-OF-BASE
arms.note: lines are counted from zero

arms.name: M-UTIL-LINE-OF-BREAK
arms.note: a carriage return is counted as the line break instead of the newline

arms.name: M-UTIL-FIRST-LINE-CUT
arms.note: the first line keeps the break that ends it

arms.name: M-UTIL-FIRST-LINE-WHOLE
arms.note: a text without a break has an empty first line

arms.name: M-UTIL-FIRST-LINE-CR
arms.note: the carriage return of a CRLF break stays in the first line

arms.name: M-UTIL-FIRST-LINE-NO-BREAK-CR
arms.note: the carriage return of a text without a line feed is dropped

arms.name: M-UTIL-BLANK-RANGE
arms.note: vertical tab and form feed are not white space

arms.name: M-UTIL-BLANK-EMPTY
arms.note: the empty text is not blank

arms.name: M-UTIL-IDENT-START-UNDERSCORE
arms.note: an underscore does not start an identifier

arms.name: M-UTIL-IDENT-CHAR-DIGIT
arms.note: the digit nine does not continue an identifier

arms.name: M-UTIL-IDENTIFIER-START
arms.note: an identifier may start with a digit

arms.name: M-UTIL-IDENTIFIER-REST
arms.note: only the first character of an identifier is checked

arms.name: M-UTIL-QUOTE-DQ
arms.note: a double quote in the text is written unescaped

arms.name: M-UTIL-QUOTE-BS
arms.note: a backslash in the text is written once

arms.name: M-UTIL-QUOTE-NL
arms.note: a newline is written as the escape of a carriage return

arms.name: M-UTIL-QUOTE-BACKSPACE
arms.note: a backspace is no longer written as its short escape

arms.name: M-UTIL-QUOTE-FORMFEED
arms.note: a form feed is no longer written as its short escape

arms.name: M-UTIL-QUOTE-CONTROL
arms.note: a control character is written raw, which no JSON reader accepts

arms.name: M-UTIL-CHAR-COUNT
arms.note: each occurrence counts twice

arms.name: M-UTIL-BEFORE-CUT
arms.note: the part before the delimiter keeps its first character

arms.name: M-UTIL-BEFORE-MISSING
arms.note: a missing delimiter gives an empty string instead of null

arms.name: M-UTIL-BEFORE-PLAIN
arms.note: a missing delimiter empties the text instead of leaving it

arms.name: M-UTIL-AFTER-CUT
arms.note: the part after the delimiter skips one character of it, not all of it

arms.name: M-UTIL-AFTER-MISSING
arms.note: a missing delimiter gives an empty string instead of null

arms.name: M-UTIL-AFTER-PLAIN
arms.note: a missing delimiter empties the text instead of leaving it

arms.name: M-UTIL-AFTER-LAST-CUT
arms.note: the part after the last delimiter skips one character of it, not all of it

arms.name: M-UTIL-AFTER-LAST-LAST
arms.note: the first delimiter is used where the last one is meant

arms.name: M-UTIL-AFTER-LAST-MISSING
arms.note: a missing delimiter gives an empty string instead of null

arms.name: M-UTIL-AFTER-LAST-PLAIN
arms.note: a missing delimiter empties the text instead of leaving it

arms.name: M-UTIL-FIRST-SPLIT-FIRST
arms.note: the last delimiter is used where the first one is meant

arms.name: M-UTIL-FIRST-SPLIT-MISSING
arms.note: a missing delimiter gives two empty parts instead of null

arms.name: M-UTIL-LAST-SPLIT-LAST
arms.note: the first delimiter is used where the last one is meant

arms.name: M-UTIL-LAST-SPLIT-MISSING
arms.note: a missing delimiter gives two empty parts instead of null

arms.name: M-UTIL-EXTRACT-START
arms.note: the extract starts inside a multi-character opening delimiter

arms.name: M-UTIL-EXTRACT-CLOSE-AFTER
arms.note: a closing delimiter before the opening one ends the extract

arms.name: M-UTIL-EXTRACT-NO-OPEN
arms.note: a missing opening delimiter lets the extract start at the text start

arms.name: M-UTIL-EXTRACT-NO-CLOSE
arms.note: a missing closing delimiter gives an empty extract instead of null

arms.name: M-UTIL-COMPARE-INT-LESS
arms.note: a smaller integer that is one below compares as equal

arms.name: M-UTIL-COMPARE-INT-MORE
arms.note: a larger integer that is one above compares as equal

arms.name: M-UTIL-COMPARE-INT-EQUAL
arms.note: equal integers compare as larger

arms.name: M-UTIL-COMPARE-STRING-LESS
arms.note: the smaller string compares as equal

arms.name: M-UTIL-COMPARE-STRING-MORE
arms.note: the larger string compares as equal

arms.name: M-UTIL-COMPARE-STRING-EQUAL
arms.note: equal strings compare as larger

arms.name: M-UTIL-COMPARE-STRING-CASE
arms.note: the order follows the letter, not the code unit
